# Import data

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Libraries
library(readxl)
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(dplyr)

metabolic_result_full_community_path <- "../data/METABOLIC_result_full_community.xlsx"

df_HMMHitNum <- read_excel(metabolic_result_full_community_path, sheet = "HMMHitNum")
df_FunctionHit <- read_excel(metabolic_result_full_community_path, sheet = "FunctionHit")
df_KEGGModuleStepHit <- read_excel(metabolic_result_full_community_path, sheet = "KEGGModuleStepHit")
df_dbCAN2Hit <- read_excel(metabolic_result_full_community_path, sheet = "dbCAN2Hit")
df_MEROPSHit <- read_excel(metabolic_result_full_community_path, sheet = "MEROPSHit")
```

```{r}
df_HMMHitNum <- df_HMMHitNum %>% 
  clean_names() %>% 
  rename(gene_function = 'function')
```

Define microbe names for later use throughout
```{r}
microbes <- c(
  "chitinophaga",
  "koribacteraceae",
  "parvibaculum",
  "propionicimonas",
  "rhodomicrobium",
  "rhodopseudomonas",
  "sporomusa",
  "terracidiphilus"
)
```


# Check for duplicates

```{r}
# Source - https://stackoverflow.com/a/16907515
# Posted by Kikapp
# Retrieved 2026-10-28, License - CC BY-SA 3.0

n_occur <- data.frame(table(df_FunctionHit$Category))
n_occur[n_occur$Freq > 1,]

n_occur <- data.frame(table(df_FunctionHit$Function))
n_occur[n_occur$Freq > 1,]

n_occur <- data.frame(table(df_FunctionHit$Gene.abbreviation))
n_occur[n_occur$Freq > 1,]

```

Category and Function columns have duplicates, but Gene.abbreviation doesn't.

# Create and compare functional profiles

```{r}
df_presence_matrix <- df_FunctionHit %>%
  select(
    Gene.abbreviation,
    ends_with("Function.presence")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      ends_with("Function.presence"),
      ~ as.integer(.x == "Present")
    )
  ) %>%
  rename_with(
    ~ str_remove(.x, "\\.Function\\.presence$"),
    ends_with("Function.presence")
  )

presence_matrix <- df_presence_matrix %>%
  select(-Gene.abbreviation) %>%
  as.matrix() %>%
  `rownames<-`(df_presence_matrix$Gene.abbreviation)
```

## Jaccard similarity

```{r}
library(vegan)

# Rows = microbes; columns = functions
microbe_matrix <- t(presence_matrix)

# Jaccard similarity
jaccard_similarity <- 1 - as.matrix(
  vegdist(microbe_matrix, method = "jaccard", binary = TRUE)
)

round(jaccard_similarity, 2)

jaccard_similarity %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("microbe1") %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -microbe1,
    names_to = "microbe2",
    values_to = "similarity"
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = microbe1, y = microbe2, fill = similarity)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(similarity, 2)), size = 3) +
  coord_equal() +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "white",
    high = "steelblue",
    limits = c(0, 1)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Functional Similarity Between Microbes",
    subtitle = "Jaccard similarity based on detected functions",
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL,
    fill = "Similarity"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )
```

# Identify potential metabolic connections

## Pivot data for analysis

```{r}
presence_long <- df_HMMHitNum %>%
  select(
    gene_abbreviation,
    ends_with("_hmm_presence")
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = ends_with("_hmm_presence"),
    names_to = "microbe",
    names_pattern = "(.*)_hmm_presence",
    values_to = "presence"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    present = as.integer(presence == "Present")
  )
```

```{r}
# 1. Create a table of detected functions and their reactions
reaction_info <- df_HMMHitNum %>%
  mutate(function_id = row_number()) %>%
  select(
    function_id,
    gene_abbreviation,
    reaction,
    substrate,
    product
  )

# 2. Identify the functions detected in each microbe
detected_functions <- presence_long %>%
  filter(present == 1) %>%
  left_join(
    reaction_info,
    by = "gene_abbreviation"
  )

# 3. Expand products into one metabolite per row
producers <- detected_functions %>%
  filter(!is.na(product), product != "N/A") %>%
  separate_longer_delim(product, delim = ";") %>%
  mutate(metabolite = str_trim(product)) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(metabolite),
    metabolite != "",
    metabolite != "N/A"
  ) %>%
  select(
    producer = microbe,
    produced_by = gene_abbreviation,
    metabolite
  )

# 4. Expand substrates into one metabolite per row
consumers <- detected_functions %>%
  filter(!is.na(substrate), substrate != "N/A") %>%
  separate_longer_delim(substrate, delim = ";") %>%
  mutate(metabolite = str_trim(substrate)) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(metabolite),
    metabolite != "",
    metabolite != "N/A"
  ) %>%
  select(
    consumer = microbe,
    consumed_by = gene_abbreviation,
    metabolite
  )

# 5. Match potential producer-consumer pairs
candidate_links <- producers %>%
  inner_join(consumers, by = "metabolite") %>%
  filter(producer != consumer) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  arrange(metabolite, producer, consumer)

# Identify metabolites each microbe can produce
microbe_products <- producers %>%
  distinct(microbe = producer, metabolite)

# Remove connections where the consumer can also produce
# the same metabolite
candidate_links_filtered <- candidate_links %>%
  anti_join(
    microbe_products,
    by = c(
      "consumer" = "microbe",
      "metabolite" = "metabolite"
    )
  )

candidate_links_filtered
```

## Summarize potential connections

```{r}
relationship_summary <- candidate_links %>%
  # Remove exact duplicate candidate links
  distinct(
    producer, produced_by, metabolite,
    consumer, consumed_by
  ) %>%
  group_by(producer, consumer) %>%
  summarise(
    metabolites = paste(
      sort(unique(metabolite)),
      collapse = "; "
    ),
    n_metabolites = n_distinct(metabolite),
    n_candidate_links = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # arrange(desc(n_metabolites), desc(n_candidate_links))
  arrange(producer, consumer)

relationship_summary
```

```{r}

ggplot(
  relationship_summary,
  aes(x = consumer, y = producer, fill = n_metabolites)
) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = n_metabolites), size = 3) +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "white",
    high = "steelblue",
    name = "Distinct\nmetabolites"
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
  scale_y_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "Potential Metabolic Connections Between Microbes",
    subtitle = "Number of distinct matched metabolites",
    x = "Potential consumer",
    y = "Potential producer"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )
```

## Filter for unique producers
Only show producer-consumer relationships where that producer is the sole producer of the metabolite in the community.
```{r}
# Identify metabolites that have exactly one microbial producer
unique_producers <- producers %>%
  distinct(producer, produced_by, metabolite) %>%
  group_by(metabolite) %>%
  filter(n_distinct(producer) == 1) %>%
  ungroup()

# Match uniquely produced metabolites with consumers
candidate_links_unique <- unique_producers %>%
  inner_join(
    consumers,
    by = "metabolite"
  ) %>%
  filter(producer != consumer) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  arrange(metabolite, producer, consumer)

relationship_summary_unique <- candidate_links_unique %>%
  distinct(
    producer, metabolite,
    consumer, consumed_by
  ) %>%
  group_by(producer, consumer) %>%
  summarise(
    metabolites = paste(
      sort(unique(metabolite)),
      collapse = "; "
    ),
    n_metabolites = n_distinct(metabolite),
    n_candidate_links = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(producer, consumer)

relationship_summary_unique
```

```{r}
ggplot(
  relationship_summary_unique,
  aes(x = consumer, y = producer, fill = n_metabolites)
) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = n_metabolites), size = 3) +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "white",
    high = "steelblue",
    name = "Distinct\nmetabolites"
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
  scale_y_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "Potential Metabolic Connections Between Microbes",
    subtitle = "Only metabolites with a single identified producer",
    x = "Potential consumer",
    y = "Potential producer"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )
```


## Filter for unique consumers
```{r}
# Identify metabolites that have exactly one microbial consumer
unique_consumers <- consumers %>%
  distinct(consumer, consumed_by, metabolite) %>%
  group_by(metabolite) %>%
  filter(n_distinct(consumer) == 1) %>%
  ungroup()

# Match uniquely consumed metabolites with producers
candidate_links_unique_consumer <- producers %>%
  inner_join(
    unique_consumers,
    by = "metabolite"
  ) %>%
  filter(producer != consumer) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  arrange(metabolite, producer, consumer)

relationship_summary_unique_consumer <- candidate_links_unique_consumer %>%
  distinct(
    producer, produced_by,
    metabolite,
    consumer, consumed_by
  ) %>%
  group_by(producer, consumer) %>%
  summarise(
    metabolites = paste(
      sort(unique(metabolite)),
      collapse = "; "
    ),
    n_metabolites = n_distinct(metabolite),
    n_candidate_links = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(producer, consumer)

relationship_summary_unique_consumer
```

## Filter for unique consumer and producer
```{r}
# Identify metabolites that have exactly one microbial consumer and one producer
candidate_links_both_unique <- unique_producers %>%
  inner_join(
    unique_consumers,
    by = "metabolite"
  ) %>%
  # filter(producer != consumer) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  arrange(metabolite, producer, consumer)

candidate_links_both_unique
```

There aren't any microbes that uniquely consume a metabolite that's uniquely produced by a different microbe, but rhodopseudomonas uniquely produces and consumes [SoxY protein]-S-disulfanyl-L-cysteine

# Filter for unique modules in KEGGModuleStepHit
For each microbe, find what modules it has that no other microbe has.
```{r}
get_unique_kegg <- function(df, microbe) {

  target_col <- paste0(microbe, ".Module.step.presence")

  df %>% 
    filter(
      .data[[target_col]] == "Present",
      if_all(
        ends_with(".Module.step.presence") & 
          !all_of(target_col),
        ~ .x == "Absent"
      )
    )
}

unique_kegg <- 
  set_names(microbes) %>% 
  map(~ get_unique_kegg(df_KEGGModuleStepHit, .x))

unique_kegg_all <- 
  imap_dfr(
    unique_kegg,
    ~ .x %>% 
      select(Module.step, Module, KO.id, Module.Category) %>% 
      mutate(microbe = .y)
  ) %>% 
  select(microbe, Module.step, Module, KO.id, Module.Category) %>% 
  arrange(microbe, Module.step)

unique_kegg_all %>% 
  select(microbe, Module, everything())
```
